tools.description:
Rate a previous answer so the semantic layer learns which tables and measures work.

    Call this once per answered question when the user says the answer was right or wrong.
    Example: feedback({"query_id": "q_8f21", "rating": 5, "comment": "the 5000 rounding was right"})
tools.name: feedback

outputSchema.description:

``user_id`` is here so a misissued token shows up in the first call instead of in an empty
result. Once the pipeline lands, the user id moves into the history and audit records.

fix.description: What to do instead, right now.
fix.title: Fix

user_id.description: The authenticated caller the server saw.

    Example: find_data({"question": "credit limit by customer status"})

tools.description:
Page the rest of a result that `query` returned with a handle.

    Call this only with a `handle` from a previous answer, never to re-run a query: the rows come
    from the cached result, so a repeated call is cheap.
    Example: get_more({"handle": "h_8f21", "offset": 100, "limit": 100})

tools.description:
Run one query spec and get a summary, a small sample and a handle. This is the main tool.

    Send a spec, never SQL. The server lints it, enforces time bounds and partition pruning, picks
    the source and the unit conversions, and answers with a summary plus a `handle` you page with
    `get_more`. Errors carry `code`, `problem` and an exact `fix`.
    Example: query({"spec": {"from": "customers", "select": [{"measure": "credit_limit_r5000",
    "agg": "avg"}], "group_by": ["customer_status"], "limit": 50}})

Agg.description: Aggregation over a measure. ``None`` on a select item means the measure's own default.
Agg.title: Agg

Filter.description: One predicate. Hebrew/English labels are fine: the server resolves them to source values.

value.description: A single value, or a list for op 'in' (any length) and 'range' (exactly 2).
value.title: Value

Filter.title: Filter

FilterOp.description: Comparison on one column: a list for ``in``/``range``, a scalar for everything else.
FilterOp.title: FilterOp

agg.description: Aggregation; omit for the measure default.

alias.description: Output column name; defaults to measure_agg.
alias.title: Alias

measure.description: A measure name from the semantic layer.
measure.title: Measure

OrderBy.description: Sort key: a column, a measure name or a select alias, plus a direction.

by.description: A selected column, measure or alias, or a group_by key.
by.title: By

OrderBy.title: OrderBy

QuerySpec.description: One query, as an agent sends it. Frozen: a validated spec never changes under the server.

dry_run.description: Plan and lint, return no rows.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

fresh.description: Skip the cache and fetch from the source now.
fresh.title: Fresh

from.description: Table (or endpoint/index) name from the catalog.
from.title: From

joins.description: Approved join names from the semantic layer; never a join condition.
joins.title: Joins

limit.description: Row cap; the server adds its own cap when this is missing.
limit.title: Limit

QuerySpec.title: QuerySpec

TimeMode.description:
The time intent. The agent says what it means; the server picks the column.

``events_in_range`` asks about a period (event time). ``new_since`` asks what is new since a
previous fetch (ingestion time, with a derived bound so late rows are not missed).
TimeMode.title: TimeMode

TimeSpec.description:
The time window intent, never a column (the server maps it: DESIGN section 6).

``events_in_range`` needs ``last`` (a trailing window from the execution time) **or** an
absolute ``from``/``to``. ``new_since`` needs ``since`` and is answered on the ingestion time
with a derived bound, so nothing is missed when a row arrives late.
TimeSpec.title: TimeSpec
